title: Functions of several variables
goal: Picture a two-variable function $z = f(x, y)$ as a 3D landscape height above an $(x, y)$ map, and find which $(x, y)$ inputs are allowed (domain) and which heights $z$ come out (range).

beforeThis.skill: To find the domain of $f(x, y)$, look for the usual three troublemakers: denominators cannot be $0$, inside of $\sqrt{\phantom{x}}$ must be $\ge 0$, and inside of $\ln(\phantom{x})$ must be $> 0$.

questions.asking: Read the output intervals of $f$ and $g$ from their graphs on $[-1, 1]$, then determine which $x$-inputs can be fed into $f(g(x))$ and what outputs result.
questions.statement:
Single-variable functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are sketched below. Both have domain $[-1, 1]$.

Based on the sketches, find the following.

  1. The range of $f(x)$,
  2. the range of $g(x)$,
  3. the domain of $f(g(x))$, and
  4. the range of $f(g(x))$.

figures.alt: Two side-by-side graphs on the domain [-1, 1]: on the left, y = f(x) oscillates between a minimum of -10 and a maximum of 10, passing through (0, 0); on the right, y = g(x) is a upper semicircle on [-1, 1] ranging from y = 0 at x = -1 and x = 1 up to y = 1 at x = 0.

questions.asking: State the set of all pairs $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ for which $f(x, y) = \sqrt{4x^2 + y^2}$ is defined, and the set of all output values it produces.
questions.statement:
Find the domain and range of the function

$$f(x, y) = \sqrt{4x^2 + y^2}.$$

questions.asking: State realistic sets of possible values for advertising spending $a$, unit price $p$, and resulting unit sales $D(a, p)$.
questions.statement:
If a company spends $a$ dollars on advertisements, and sells the advertised product at $p$ dollars each, then the number of units that will be sold is given as a function $D(a, p)$.

Give a sensible model domain and range.
